articles.title: Star Trek's 3 Versions Of Captain James T. Kirk: The Definitive Ranking
articles.summary: The easy way to rank the three live-action versions of Kirk would be to simply declare William Shatner the winner and move on. After all, he's the actor who delivered us one of science fiction's most enduring characters.
body: Captain James T. Kirk has been one of television's defining heroes for nearly 60 years. For some fans, he'll always look and sound like William Shatner. Others grew up with Chris Pine's brash, Kelvin Timeline captain. And for a new generation discovering Star Trek through Strange New Worlds, Paul Wesley is steadily making the role his own.

None of the three actors is playing exactly the same man. Shatner established the legend. Pine explored how a different upbringing could shape the same extraordinary leader. Wesley is showing us the ambitious young officer still growing into the captain who would one day command the Enterprise. Together, they give us a fuller picture of the human being sitting in that captain’s chair, flaws and all.
With that in mind, here's how the three live-action versions of Captain James T. Kirk rank.
points: The easy way to rank the three live-action versions of Kirk would be to simply declare William Shatner the winner and move on.
After all, he's the actor who delivered us one of science fiction's most enduring characters.
Kirk has been one of television's defining heroes for nearly 60 years.
Others grew up with Chris Pine's brash, Kelvin Timeline captain.

articles.summary: It’s no secret that handheld gaming is in a bit of a renaissance right now. Ushered in by the Nintendo Switch and carried forward by the Steam Deck and more powerful handheld PCs like the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, there’s never been more options for playing games on the small screen, whether that’s away…
body: Alongside these mainstream offerings are another class of handhelds aimed more at the past than the future. In particular, Android-powered dual-screen handhelds like the AYN Thor look to offer hardware designed for emulating the Nintendo DS and 3DS. This week, Retroid entered the fray teasing out its upcoming Pocket Duo, and today we now know how much it will cost.

The Retroid Pocket Duo will cost $270 for the flagship model, which comes with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, though there’s a coupon to knock $20 off when pre-ordering. articles.title: Nintendo Finally Adds Some Life To The Switch 2
articles.summary: Both of Nintendo's Switch consoles have been cursed with deafening silence in their menus and eShops. But the latest version 23.0.0 update for the Switch 2 at least injects a little bit of personality and nostalgia into one of the platform's menus, bringing back music for the Mii Maker.
body: When you create a Mii in the Switch 2's system settings, the familiar Mii Channel music from the Wii now plays in the background. A music settings button on the top left also lets you change the track to the 3DS or Wii U Mii Maker music (the tracks are generically named "Track 1," Track 2," and "Track 3").
Certain Nintendo fans feel that the company's platforms have lost some of their soul with the lack of music and visual themes, so this update, as small as it is, can be taken as a nice gesture.

Unfortunately, both Switch platforms are still without any eShop background music or visual themes. Nintendo omitted these menu elements for the first Switch to save processing power and allow users to quickly navigate the UI to start their games. At the very least, it seems like the Switch 2 has some extra juice to accommodate some Mii music.

The Switch 2 firmware update allows users to share their Miis through QR codes. While Miis might not be as big a deal for Nintendo as they were in the Mii days, the cartoony avatars are still very much a part of modern games like Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream and the upcoming Nintendo Switch Sports Resort.
points: Both of Nintendo's Switch consoles have been cursed with deafening silence in their menus and eShops.
But the latest version 23.0.0 update for the Switch 2 at least injects a little bit of personality and nostalgia into one of the platform's menus, bringing back music for the Mii Maker.

articles.title: Hasbro Responds to DHS Using AI Optimus Prime in Deportation Posts
articles.summary: Hasbro has responded to the Department of Homeland Security’s recent AI-generated social media posts that used the likeness of the Hasbro-owned character, Transformers’ Optimus Prime, to promote its deportation program, stating that DHS’ posts were created without their consent.
body: One DHS ad is an AI-generated fake movie poster for “Transformers: Age of Deportation” featuring Optimus Prime with DHS and ICE insignia.

A second DHS post showed Optimus face to face with a Sikh man, declaring, “Self-deport or find out” and “America for Americans. Get off our roads; you don’t know how to drive Mr Singh.” That post – which the DHS has since deleted – was widely blasted as being blatantly racist.

“Optimus Prime is a beloved character who represents humility, leadership, compassion and justice. Hasbro is aware of the recent posts using his likeness. These posts were done without permission and do not represent the Transformers brand or Hasbro.”
As Entertainment Weekly points out, the DHS’ Optimus Prime spots were also criticized for coming on the heels of the death of Peter Cullen, the actor who voiced Optimus for decades.

articles.title: Gary Larson's 10 Best The Far Side Comics, Ranked
articles.summary: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips? The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — and sometimes even just one panel — to express a joke or a sentiment.
body: Yet, we’ve seen it do so much more than that. Characters like Snoopy and Garfield have become part of the fabric of our culture, which means comic strips are capable of greatness. And since greatness is possible, what, then, makes a comic strip great?

The first instinct is to go for something “deep.” Comic strips like Peanuts and Calvin and Hobbes occasionally ventured outside of comedy to examine the world and say something thoughtful about it. But that’s not the case for other comic strips that don’t go deep. For Garfield, I’d argue greatness would come down to a really clever, relatable gag. For something like Prince Valiant, which specialized in highly detailed, picturesque images, I imagine greatness would relate to visual appeal.
So what would the measure of greatness be for Gary Larson’s The Far Side?
points: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips?
The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — and sometimes even just one panel — to express a joke or a sentiment.

articles.title: 33 Years Later, the Best Sci-Fi Show of the '90s Is Officially Streaming for Free
articles.summary: Created by Chris Carter, The X-Files is about a pair of FBI agents who investigate cases involving the paranormal — and Carter interpreted “paranormal” very broadly. The agents investigated everything from aliens to urban legends to ghosts to many other strange goings-on.
body: For some decades, it might be a bit tough to determine what the best sci-fi TV show was. The 1960s had both Star Trek and The Twilight Zone, which is a really difficult choice. For the 1970s, Battlestar Galactica probably wins, but it has some competition from Space: 1999 and The Six Million Dollar Man. The 1980s had Star Trek: The Next Generation, but V gives that show a run for its money. In the 1990s, however, one show stands out as the best sci-fi series of the decade without any serious contender — and that show is currently free to stream on Pluto TV.

Mulder was the true believer of the pair. His sister was abducted by aliens when he was a kid and he believed that all kinds of spectacular things were possible. Meanwhile, Scully was the skeptic, a medical doctor with a rigid scientific viewpoint who needed to be convinced of everything. That yin and yang was the genius of The X-Files. It allowed everyone in the audience — the believers and skeptics alike — to identify with at least one of the two main characters.

articles.title: Wardogs’ Massive Start On Steam Undercut By Brutal Server Queues [Update]
articles.summary: Update: A hotfix has now been released for Wardogs that targets the ongoing server issues. If you're logged in and stuck in a queue, you'll need to close the game to download the update, which will then send you back into a queue once you log in again.
body: More players will be let in as the issues are resolved, but no specific timetable is provided for how long that could take. Alongside the long queues, the patch targets issues with joining servers and an issue causing players to be kicked from matches.

"We will be actively monitoring the ongoing situation post hotfix and will be working through the night to see this resolved," the developer wrote in a post on Steam. "We apologize for the inconvenience this has caused."

Original story: A big new military FPS, Wardogs (not to be confused with the 2016 Jonah Hill/Miles Teller crime-comedy War Dogs) launched today in early access on Steam, and it's off to a hot start. The shooter reached 300,000 peak concurrent users on Steam right out of the gate and the $40 game is currently Steam's No. 1 best-seller. Pretty impressive for a game that the developer told you not to buy.

Given the flood of players, developer Bulkhead instituted a server queue system, and this quickly became something of a meme on social media. Players shared screenshots of the queue and their place in it--some people reported having more than 300,000 people in line in front of them. Yeesh.

articles.title: 24 Years Later, the 220-Episode Action Classic That Defined a Generation Is Free to Stream on YouTube
articles.summary: Some anime feel less like TV shows than cultural events woven into the fabric of our childhoods. Dragon Ball Z introduced generations of viewers to the idea that a fight could somehow last 12 episodes and still leave you breathless.
body: One of the greatest among them and a major part of the “ Big Three,” Naruto is the hardest to ignore. The original series, available to stream for free on Pluto TV right now, follows the young Naruto Uzumaki on his quest to become his village’s Hokage, its most respected ninja. His brash, reckless personality makes him prone to trouble, while the Nine-Tailed Fox sealed inside him has made him an outcast among villagers who fear the creature’s power. It’s a volatile combination for a lead, yet it ultimately anchored what would become one of the biggest anime franchises in the world.

At first, Naruto presents itself as a show about ninjas hurling increasingly ridiculous techniques at each other. As the series progresses, it becomes a surprisingly earnest story about loneliness, friendship, perseverance, and the desire to be recognized. For Naruto, becoming Hokage was never really about political ambition or raw power. It was a lonely child's desperate blueprint for survival. For a kid raised on cold stares and averted eyes, that title was the only guaranteed way he could force a village that treated him like a curse to finally acknowledge his existence.
points: Some anime feel less like TV shows than cultural events woven into the fabric of our childhoods.
Dragon Ball Z introduced generations of viewers to the idea that a fight could somehow last 12 episodes and still leave you breathless.

articles.title: How to increase your inventory in Valheim
articles.summary: Whether you're a Valheim veteran or playing for the first time, at some point you're going to stop and ask "Is there any way to increase the size of my inventory? And finally, as of Valheim 1.0, the answer is yes, you can!
body: Inventory size in Valheim is famously small, with just eight hotbar slots and 24 inventory slots. Especially since worn armor takes up slots, your inventory is going to be full quickly and constantly, making it tough to haul back all the loot and resources you find in the world. At long last, there's something you can do about it.

Visit Haldor. The NPC merchant in the Black Forest now sells two inventory upgrades in exchange for coins, with each upgrade giving you an extra row in your inventory, meaning you can add a total of 16 extra slots.

If you're new to Valheim, you may not have run into Haldor yet, and he can be hard to find. The vendor will only appear in the Black Forest biome, and there's not many ways to find him besides just going out into the world and looking.

You can also try putting your Valheim world seed into a third-party utility like the Valheim World Generator, though it may not show Haldor's location reliably until it's been updated to support Valheim 1.0.
points: Whether you're a Valheim veteran or playing for the first time, at some point you're going to stop and ask "Is there any way to increase the size of my inventory?
And finally, as of Valheim 1.0, the answer is yes, you can!

articles.title: Star Wars Zero Company gets much-needed first patch so you won't miss shots with a 100% chance to hit any more
articles.summary: The main thing preventing me from playing Star Wars Zero Company in its iron man "beskar" mode is cowardice, but the second thing preventing me from doing that has been the state of the game at launch.
body: Fortunately, a 1.1 patch is here, and the first patch note is "Fixed various crash issues." Following that, "Fixed an issue where Beskar saves were temporarily deleted" and "Fixed a crash issue for Beskar mode."

There's also a fix for "an issue where shots can be missed, even when the chance to hit is 100%." I've been assuming that ZCOM was rounding up the numbers and actually I'd been missing 97% chance shots the several times I completely whiffed a point-blank sure thing in my playthrough, so it'll be nice to actually land those attacks instead.

The other main bug I experienced was overwatch not triggering even when enemies jog through multiple targeting cones on their turn. That doesn't seem to have been addressed, although several other bugs involving overwatch triggering against units outside the targeting cone or behind solid objects have. Maybe I'll wait one more patch before turning on the beskar mode then.

articles.title: Metroid Dread studio MercurySteam appears to confirm it's making Metroid Ravenous, addressing a lingering question from yesterday's Nintendo Direct
articles.summary: Spanish studio MercurySteam - the developer of Metroid Dread - seems to be the studio behind yesterday's Nintendo Direct showcase stopper, Metroid Ravenous.
body: Questions were raised after the Direct showcase because, despite the obvious visual similarities between Metroid Dread and Ravenous, MercurySteam's name did not appear in the Ravenous trailer or on any associated press gumpf. MercurySteam's social accounts were also quiet following the event.

I sought clarification from Nintendo and from MercurySteam this morning because of this, but heard nothing back - though this silence is not unusual for Nintendo, which often doesn't disclose developers until close to a game's release.

Nonetheless, MercurySteam appears to have ended speculation today by retweeting yesterday's Metroid Ravenous trailer with a ninja emoji and a heart emoji, presumably signalling some kind of stealth development situation. The same trailer was shared on LinkedIn by the company moments ago as well.

Metroid Ravenous seems to closely follow the Metroid Dread template, offering a side-on Metroid adventure, albeit one that plays with perspective a lot. Ravenous appears more colourful and less oppressive than Dread, and its montage of energetic gameplay lit-up Nintendo's Direct yesterday afternoon.

videos.title: Xbox Saves Kojima's Physint from PlayStation Cancellation - IGN Daily Fix
videos.summary: Hideo Kojima's upcoming spy project, Physint, is moving from PlayStation to Xbox. Announced by Kojima, the move was apparently due to Physint's potentially cancellation by Sony, who may have been scared off by Death Stranding 2's low sales compared to the original.
points: Hideo Kojima's upcoming spy project, Physint, is moving from PlayStation to Xbox.
Announced by Kojima, the move was apparently due to Physint's potentially cancellation by Sony, who may have been scared off by Death Stranding 2's low sales compared to the original.
Xbox has now signed a publishing deal with Kojima Productions, and will now be publishing both Physint and the upcoming horror game, OD.
In other news, Nintendo is giving back to their fans—sort of—by way of a sale discounting select games, hardware, and accessories like amiibo.
